facts.note: what recipes' "requires" is checked against (docs/requires.md), with the OCLP hardware profile's CPU flags. Not yet proven on hardware: OCLP's model data and the 12,1's recorded facts; a capture from the Mac itself confirms or replaces every fact here

esp.note: none: no harvested EFI for this model. golden-run builds its EFI from the pinned OCLP source (pipeline/stages/build-efi.py); the legacy Tahoe-first runner (pipeline/run), the only reader of this key, does not build this model

sources.model, board_id, firmware_vendor: OCLP datasets/smbios_data.py MacBookPro12,1 (Board ID Mac-E43C1C25D4880AD6, SecureBootModel None: no T1/T2)
sources.cpu.name: Intel's i5-5257U, the base CPU of MacBookPro12,1 (assumed; a capture from the Mac replaces it with sysctl machdep.cpu.brand_string)
sources.cpu.flags: the 12,1's recorded facts (the Haswell leaf-1 flags): leaf 1 is the same on Haswell and Broadwell; OCLP datasets/example_data.py MacBookPro111_Stock
sources.cpu.leafs: Broadwell's CPUID leaf 7 features in machdep.cpu.leaf7_features names (AVX2, BMI1/2, SMEP, SMAP, INVPCID, RDSEED, ADX, ERMS); HLE and RTM (TSX) left out until the Mac shows them (QEMU Broadwell-noTSX)
sources.pci: only the devices OCLP's patch-set detection reads: the GPU (Iris 6100, 8086:162b, OCLP device_probe Broadwell IDs) and the Wi-Fi card (14e4:43ba, BCM43602, assumed: any AirportBrcmNIC chipset gives the same patch sets); an ioreg capture from the Mac replaces the list
sources.pcie_webcam: OCLP efi_builder/misc.py treats every Haswell to Kaby Lake MacBook as having the PCIe FaceTime camera; a capture from the Mac confirms
sources.t1_chip: OCLP smbios_data: SecureBootModel None (no T1, no T2)
sources.selected patch sets: tools/oclp-hardware/profile.py: OCLP's own HardwarePatchsetDetection on this profile for Darwin 25 (the method reproduces profiles/mbp92.json byte for byte)

efi_build.source: pinned OCLP source and payloads; no installed OCLP application

opencore_reasons.kext:AppleHSSPISupport.kext: OCLP (misc.py _topcase_handling, Broadwell to Kaby Lake MacBooks, macOS 14.4+): the SPI bus driver of this Mac's internal keyboard and trackpad, removed from macOS 14.4; without it they are dead
opencore_reasons.kext:AppleHSSPIHIDDriver.kext: OCLP (misc.py _topcase_handling): the HID driver on the SPI bus for the internal keyboard and trackpad (with AppleHSSPISupport)
opencore_reasons.kext:AppleTopCaseInjector.kext: OCLP (misc.py _topcase_handling): codeless matching that attaches Apple's top-case stack to the SPI keyboard and trackpad
opencore_reasons.kext:AppleCameraInterface.kext: OCLP (misc.py _webcam_handling, Haswell to Kaby Lake MacBooks): the PCIe FaceTime HD camera driver, removed from macOS 14; a capture from the Mac confirms the camera is PCIe
opencore_reasons.kext:IOS3XeFamily.kext: OCLP (storage.py, Haswell to Kaby Lake models): Apple's S1X/S3X SSD family, removed from macOS 14 beta 2; UNTRACED: OCLP adds it for every model of this range, a capture from the Mac shows whether this Mac's SSD is AHCI or NVMe (trace: ioreg IOAHCIBlockStorage or IONVMeController)
opencore_reasons.kext:CryptexFixup.kext: opencore-mbp121 (OCLP leaves it out on AVX2 CPUs): the image's modified OS cryptex needs its APFS root-hash patch, or the graft fails (graftdmg 80) and the boot stops before userspace (QEMU 2026-11-17 on IvyBridge). On an AVX2 CPU it patches only with -crypt_force_avx (hao-opencore arg_reasons; disassembly of the 1.0.5 RELEASE binary)
opencore_reasons.kext:RestrictEvents.kext: OCLP (misc.py): revpatch sbvmm and revblock media (below); no f16c on this CPU (OCLP adds it on Ivy Bridge only)
opencore_reasons.kext:AirPortBrcmNIC-Tahoe.kext: OCLP Wi-Fi: Tahoe's Broadcom AirPort driver for this Mac's AirportBrcmNIC card on macOS 26/27
opencore_reasons.nvram-add:4D1FDA02-38C7-4A6A-9CC6-4BCCA8: RestrictEvents: sbvmm (reports a VMM board so software update offers this Mac updates; OCLP adds it unless a serial is set); no f16c on Broadwell
opencore_reasons.uefi-quirk:EnableVmx: OCLP (firmware.py, Haswell and Broadwell MacBooks): the firmware leaves VMX unlocked, so virtual machines in other OSes (and macOS's Hypervisor) can use VT-x
